questions.q: A doctor's duty under the law to inform the police applies to:
opts: medicolegal cases such as injuries, poisoning and suspicious deaths
questions.why: Topic 10, Community and Forensic Medicine, Ethics. MLC registration and intimation.

questions.q: Pre-eclampsia is defined as hypertension after 20 weeks of pregnancy with:
Scrub typhus, seen in Goa and other states, is transmitted by:
questions.why: Topic 6, Pathology, Microbiology and Diagnostics. Orientia tsutsugamushi; an eschar is a clue.

questions.q: Excessive scar tissue that grows beyond the margins of the original wound and does not regress is called a:
questions.why: A keloid extends beyond the wound boundary and seldom regresses; a hypertrophic scar stays within the wound margins.

questions.q: Diseases such as smallpox, measles and whooping cough, which recur in the same manner and attack a person usually only once in life, are called in §73:
questions.why: §73 groups acute diseases into individual, sporadic, epidemic and acute miasms; smallpox and measles are acute miasms of fixed character.

questions.q: According to §141, the best of all provings are those made by:
opts: the healthy, unprejudiced and sensitive physician on himself
students under the supervision of a professor
volunteers who know nothing of the drug
questions.why: §141: the best pure experiments are those the healthy, unprejudiced, sensitive physician makes on himself.

questions.q: According to §18, the sole indication guiding the choice of the remedy is:
opts: the totality of symptoms, with its accompanying circumstances
questions.why: Topic 1, Organon and Philosophy. §18: the sum of all the symptoms and circumstances is the sole indication.

questions.q: Suspicion, secretiveness, jealousy and fixed ideas are the mental features of which miasm?
questions.why: Sycotic mentals are suspicious, secretive, jealous and fixed in ideas; psora is anxious and fearful, syphilis destructive and depressed.

questions.q: Phatak's Concise Repertory of Homoeopathic Medicines was built mainly on:
questions.why: S. R. Phatak based his alphabetical repertory chiefly on C. M. Boger's Synoptic Key, enlarging it from other sources.

questions.q: Cramps in calves and toes, epileptic spasms, and complaints relieved by drinking cold water point to:
questions.why: Topic 2, Materia Medica. Cuprum: violent cramps, cold water relieves the cough.
